source_refs.note: Exercise 11.2, Question 3 (book page 211): solve graphically, parts (i)-(ii). The answer key (PDF 309) prints no answer for Q3; answers x = pi/4 and x = 0 are ours, checked. Solution book PDF 1019-1020.

blocks.explanation:
Yahan equation ko algebra se nahi, graph bana kar solve karna hai. Jahan do curves ek doosre ko kaat-te hain, wahi jawab hai.
Plan: \([0, \pi]\) par \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) ki table, dono curves, milne ka point parhna aur us ki tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\sin x = \cos x\), \(x \in [0, \pi]\).
Humein find karna hai: \([0, \pi]\) mein \(x\) ki value(s).
Tareeqa: \(f(x) = g(x)\) ko graph se solve karne ka matlab hai: \(y = f(x)\) aur \(y = g(x)\) dono ek hi axes par banao. Jahan dono curves ek doosre ko kaat-te hain (intersection), wahan dono ki unchai barabar hai, yani \(f(x) = g(x)\). Is liye un points ka x-coordinate hi equation ka hal (solution) hai. Y-coordinate jawab nahi, sirf milne ki unchai hai.

Table of values (jawab ke neeche di gayi hai)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}:\ \sin x = 0.5,\ \cos x \approx 0.87\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ \sin x \approx 0.71,\ \cos x \approx 0.71\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}:\ \sin x \approx 0.87,\ \cos x = 0.5\]
Kyun: standard angles (\(30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) waghera) ki values hamein zabani yaad hain. Table mein dekhiye: \(\pi/4\) par dono rows barabar ho jati hain. Yahi hamara ishara hai.

Dono curves banayein
\(y = \sin x\): \((0, 0)\) se upar \((\pi/2, 1)\) tak, phir neeche \((\pi, 0)\) tak. \(y = \cos x\): \((0, 1)\) se neeche \((\pi/2, 0)\) se guzar kar \((\pi, -1)\) tak.
Kyun: pehle hisse mein ek curve upar ja raha hai aur doosra neeche aa raha hai, is liye woh wahan sirf ek dafa kaat sakte hain. Dono curves ek hi scale par banayein, warna milne ka point ghalat jagah dikhega.

Milne ka point parhein
\[\text{Point of intersection} \approx \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ 0.71\right)\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\pi/4\) se pehle cosine upar hai aur baad mein sine upar. \((\pi/2, \pi]\) mein \(\sin x \ge 0\) aur \(\cos x < 0\), yani ek positive aur ek negative, woh barabar ho hi nahi sakte. Is liye doosra koi hal nahi.
Dhyan dein: jawab sirf \(x = \pi/4\) hai; 0.71 milne ki unchai hai, jawab nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\]
Kyun: \(x = \pi/4\) (\(45^{\circ}\)) par dono taraf barabar \(1/\sqrt2 \approx 0.71\) hai. Algebra se bhi: \(\tan x = 1\) ka \([0, \pi]\) mein sirf ek hal \(\pi/4\) hai.

answer_figure.alt: y = sin x and y = cos x from 0 to pi: the rising sine curve and the falling cosine curve cross once, at (pi/4, 0.71).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (i): y = sin x and y = cos x meet at x = π/4 (original drawing)

blocks.explanation:
Is equation mein ek taraf curve (\(y = \sin x\)) hai aur doosri taraf seedhi lakeer (\(y = x\)). Jahan dono milte hain, wahi hal hai.
Plan: \(x\) ko radian (saade numbers) mein lenge, dono axes par ek hi scale rakhenge, dono graph banayenge aur milne ka point parhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\sin x = x\), \(x \in [0, \pi]\).
Humein find karna hai: \([0, \pi]\) mein \(x\) ki value(s).
Tareeqa: \(f(x) = g(x)\) ko graph se solve karne ka matlab hai: \(y = f(x)\) aur \(y = g(x)\) dono ek hi axes par banao. Jahan dono curves ek doosre ko kaat-te hain (intersection), wahan dono ki unchai barabar hai, yani \(f(x) = g(x)\). Is liye un points ka x-coordinate hi equation ka hal (solution) hai. Y-coordinate jawab nahi, sirf milne ki unchai hai.
Yahan \(x\) lazmi radian mein hona chahiye, kyunke \(x\) ka muqabla \(\sin x\) jaise saade number se ho raha hai. Degree mein \(x = 30\) aur \(\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5\) ka muqabla be-maani hai.

Table of values (calculator radian mode mein)
\[x = 0.5:\ \sin x \approx 0.48\]
\[x = 1:\ \sin x \approx 0.84\]
\[x = 2:\ \sin x \approx 0.91\]
Kyun: yeh standard angles nahi, is liye values calculator se lein (radian mode zaroor check karein). Line \(y = x\) ki table to aasaan hai: jo \(x\) wohi \(y\).

Dono graph banayein
Dono axes par ek hi scale. \(y = \sin x\): \((0, 0)\) se taqreeban \((1.57, 1)\) tak upar, phir \((\pi, 0)\) tak neeche. \(y = x\): origin se guzarti \(45^{\circ}\) wali seedhi lakeer.
Kyun: barabar scale par hi \(y = x\) sahi \(45^{\circ}\) ka zaviya banati hai aur muqabla insaaf se hota hai. Agar y-axis ka scale bara rakh diya to lakeer aur curve ka faasla ghalat nazar aayega.

Milne ka point parhein
\[\text{The graphs meet only at } (0,\ 0)\]
\[x = 0\]
Kyun: table mein \(x > 0\) ke liye \(\sin x\) hamesha \(x\) se chhota hai (\(0.48 < 0.5\), \(0.84 < 1\), ...). \(x > 1\) ke baad to \(\sin x \le 1 < x\), yani lakeer bohat upar chali jati hai. Origin ke qareeb curve lakeer ko sirf chhoota hai aur phir neeche reh jata hai.
Dhyan dein: 0 ke qareeb dono graph bohat paas paas hain, is liye ghaur se dekhein; bohat se students samajhte hain ke wahan bohat se points par milte hain, lekin milna sirf origin par hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\sin 0 = 0\]
\[x = 0.5:\ 0.5 - \sin 0.5 \approx 0.02 > 0\]
Kyun: \(x = 0\) equation ko poora karta hai, aur 0 ke bilkul qareeb bhi lakeer curve se upar hai. Is liye koi doosra milne ka point nahi. Chhote angles ke liye \(\sin x \approx x\) hota hai, lekin barabar sirf \(x = 0\) par.

answer_figure.alt: y = sin x and the line y = x from 0 to pi with the same scale on both axes: the line stays above the sine curve and they meet only at the origin.
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (ii): y = sin x and y = x meet only at (0, 0) (original drawing)
